transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 57 min
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Rivermark Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Rivermark Infra), Sofia Park (Rivermark CTO)

Summary (auto): quick walk through of model library UI, how to read compatibility matrix and bench CSVs; talk about tradeoffs between latency and cost, and Redwood deployment options for PHI.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh really appreciate it. quick round robin? Jordan from Redwood, AE.
[00:07] Aisha Khan: hi Jordan, Aisha here, head of ML at Rivermark.
[00:10] Carlos Mendes: Carlos infra, hey.
[00:12] Sofia Park: Sofia, CTO. thanks for doing this.
[00:15] Jordan Lee: awesome. Priya is our systems SE — she'll do the catalog demo and bench interpretation. goal — show how you'd pick open models, read compat matrix, and plan a pilot.
[00:25] Priya Nambiar: great thanks. I'll share screen — ok can you all see the model library? (pause) someone said they can't, aish?
[00:33] Aisha Khan: yep i can see now. looks clean.
[00:35] Priya Nambiar: cool. top left is the filter bar — architecture, tokens-per-second, quantization profile, and runtime kernels. on the right is the compatibility heatmap; each row is a candidate model and columns show runtime fit, kernel mapping, latency profile, and data residency constraints. the matrix score we show is heuristic: accuracy-ish + performance match + quant safety thumb. it's not absolute but helps narrow to top 5.
[01:10] Carlos Mendes: question — how do you get the latency numbers? are these from your hosted fleet or synthetic?
[01:16] Priya Nambiar: good call. the default numbers are Redwood-verified medians from our hosted runs on the same GPU families — we also show percentile distributions and the exact benchmark CSVs for every run. if you run a local bench on your infra we can import the CSV and overlay it — that's why we ask for sequence lengths and batch distribution.
[01:35] Aisha Khan: ok that overlay is key for us since our seq lengths are short (~64) but we have spiky burst traffic. we care about p95 latency under 120ms for chat completions.
[01:46] Priya Nambiar: got it. so in the UI you can toggle to show p50/p95/p99 traces. there's also a kernel-level note — for example model X uses a fused-attn kernel on A100 which gives a lower p95 for long contexts, but for short contexts some quantized kernels are faster; the matrix tries to capture that.
[02:05] Jordan Lee: quick note — some labels might be off in the transcript, e.g., "KV cash" — we meant KV cache. you'll see typos in the export but the ideas are unchanged.
[02:14] Sofia Park: haha noted. on PHI — we can't send anything to multi-tenant hosted unless it's deidentified. what private options do you support?
[02:22] Priya Nambiar: two main paths: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in our cloud) with dedicated tenancy and no co-tenancy; or Redwood Private which can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem via our customer-managed control plane. both support KMS/HSM integrations and configurable audit logs. Dedicated is fastest to start — we can spin a dev pool for pilot.
[02:45] Carlos Mendes: for Private, does it require us to open firewall or do you provide an air-gapped package?
[02:50] Priya Nambiar: we have an on-prem bundle for air-gapped environments; it does require an initial image install and a short handshake for licensing. for VPC we talk through peering or private link.
[02:58] Aisha Khan: back to model selection — we noticed some models in the upper-right are large but run surprisingly well when quantized. how confident should we be in the quantized numbers?
[03:07] Priya Nambiar: quant numbers are extrapolated from our quantization runs; we include the delta in evaluation metrics (e.g., rouge/accuracy delta) and attach prompts used in the benchmark. for mission-critical, we recommend running a short eval set — Redwood Optimize can auto-suggest quant profiles based on your eval prompts.
[03:25] Jordan Lee: i'll add that to the follow-ups — share the Optimize guide.
[03:29] Aisha Khan: what about fallback routing? if we pick a smaller quant model for cost but then degrade, can the system fail over?
[03:36] Priya Nambiar: yes — smart routing policies let you route by latency SLO, cost, or quality. you can set canary -> fallback chains. for example route traffic to quantized model by default and route anything above a latency threshold to a higher-fidelity model. that all shows up in the runbook and console.
[03:56] Carlos Mendes: do you support prefix/KV caching across models? our app uses a lot of repeated context.
[04:01] Priya Nambiar: yes, we do prefix caching and KV cache sharing across compatible model variants — the console highlights which model pairs can share caches. note: cache compatibility is approximate; some transformers with different vocab or tokenizer won't share. sometimes the export will call it "KV cash" in the auto notes, but it's cache.
[04:18] Sofia Park: lol ok. can you walk through an example — like picking between model-a-7B-qat and model-b-13B-int8 with our workload?
[04:24] Priya Nambiar: sure. (navigates) here's model-a: low mem, great ops per second when quantized but gets a 3-5% eval quality drop on our NER prompt set. model-b-13B-int8 keeps quality and has better p95 on NVLink setups. the compat matrix marks model-a as "cost-optimal" and model-b as "latency-optimum". you can click to see the benchmark CSV; we show token breakdowns and kernel mapping rows — say you run on H100 we pick different kernels than on A100.
[04:58] Aisha Khan: you mentioned kernel mapping. can you explain the column names to me? I always get lost in the kernel names.
[05:03] Priya Nambiar: sure — kernel mapping shows which optimized kernels are used by runtime per operator: fused-attn, rotary-fast, matmul-int8, etc. we map these against hardware family; the bench CSV includes which kernel version ran during that trial. the important bit for you is that some kernels degrade more on short sequences, so the p95 shifts.
[05:23] Carlos Mendes: is the kernel map something we can influence — like force a different kernel?
[05:28] Priya Nambiar: there's a runtime flag in Dedicated and Private where you can prefer a certain kernel family, but it's advanced. usually we recommend letting the runtime pick; we can run a quick A/B with kernel overrides in the pilot.
[05:38] Jordan Lee: question from me — timeline perspective, if we do a Dedicated pilot, what's the fastest turnaround?
[05:43] Priya Nambiar: provisioning dev pool for pilot is typically 48–72 hours once we have the traffic profile and access approvals. Carlos, you'll need to confirm the IP allowlist and an SSH key for any on-prem hooks.
[05:55] Carlos Mendes: yep we can do that.
[05:57] Aisha Khan: ok what's the expected cost signal in the console? like how do we predict monthly spend if we pick model-b?
[06:05] Priya Nambiar: the console has a per-token and per-second estimate; for Dedicated we provide committed capacity quotes. for modelling costs you can export usage traces from the console and run the unit economics calc — Jordan will share a sample workbook.
[06:17] Sofia Park: security — SOC2 plus data residency. do you have a way to restrict telemetry? we don't want prompt logs leaving our region.
[06:25] Jordan Lee: yes. Private and Dedicated can disable telemetry and only keep minimal audit logs. for VPC/private we can ensure logs are stored in customer-managed S3 with lifecycle rules. we support KMS/HSM for encryption at rest and in transit. we'll send the SOC2 doc and network diagram after the call.
[06:40] Aisha Khan: excellent. about the benchmark CSV you mentioned — will it show tokenization differences? sometimes mismatched tokenizers give weird delta.
[06:47] Priya Nambiar: correct, tokenizer is a column in the CSV. we always include tokenizer hash so you can see mismatches. if you have a custom tokenizer we can ingest it and re-run a targeted bench.
[06:58] Jordan Lee: let's switch to a quick walk-through of interpreting a bench row — Priya if you can highlight the CSV columns.
[07:04] Priya Nambiar: sure — timestamp, hardware, model_id, sequence_length_dist, batch_profile, p50/p95/p99 token-latency, kernel_version, tokenizer_hash, quant_profile, eval_score_delta. look for eval_score_delta and p95 together; a low cost but a big negative delta means you might lose production quality.
[07:26] Aisha Khan: that eval delta — is it relative to base fp32? or your reference model?
[07:30] Priya Nambiar: it's relative to the model's fp32 baseline in our reference harness. we include the raw eval outputs as well.
[07:36] Carlos Mendes: if we do the pilot, will the dedicated dev pool let us run our own bench harness?
[07:40] Priya Nambiar: yes — we'll give you a bench runner container and a sample harness; you can run it and upload the results to the console which will merge overlays to the matrix.
[07:50] Sofia Park: about compliance — do you provide penetration test reports for the dedicated control plane?
[07:56] Jordan Lee: we provide SOC2 and we have a summary of third-party pen-test engagements; for enterprise we can share more detailed artifacts under an NDA.
[08:06] Aisha Khan: are there any known gotchas with quantized models and hallucination behavior? we've seen sometimes quantization causes odd output truncation in long form.
[08:15] Priya Nambiar: yes, quant artifacts can change generation distribution. that's why Redwood Optimize ties eval prompts to regression alerts. for long-form you might pin the model to a higher-fidelity variant or increase top-p sampling thresholds. we'll show you sample prompts in the pilot.
[08:30] Jordan Lee: (interrupting) quick pricing note — pilots are typically subsidized; we'll include a small usage credit for the dev Dedicated pool.
[08:38] Aisha Khan: great. Carlos — from infra side, any constraints?
[08:41] Carlos Mendes: just the usual: networking, cert pinning, and if we go on-prem we need compatibility with our HSM vendor — Thales. do you integrate with Thales?
[08:51] Priya Nambiar: we integrate with major HSM providers; Thales is supported via standard PKCS#11 or a gateway. we'll pull the integration doc into the follow-up.
[08:59] Sofia Park: okay next, concrete demo ask — can you highlight how we'd use the compatibility matrix to pick a shortlist of 3 models for our NER and summarization tasks?
[09:07] Priya Nambiar: absolutely. filters first: task signal (NER + summarization), seq length short, p95 target <120ms, quant allowed, data residency US-only. the matrix will then rank models; pick top 3 and click "compare" — that opens pairwise bench overlays and a combined cost estimate.
[09:28] Aisha Khan: can we weight quality over cost in the ranking?
[09:31] Priya Nambiar: yes there's a slider for quality vs cost vs latency. you can save a profile which becomes a rule in the playbook for rollout.
[09:40] Jordan Lee: okay folks we're at about 40 minutes — any other big blockers we should address before pilot?
[09:45] Carlos Mendes: one more — telemetry retention policy. we need 90 days on request logs but only 7 days for full prompts. can you do that?
[09:53] Jordan Lee: yes we have configurable retention per tenant; we can do 90-day minimal traces and 7-day full prompts for the pilot. we'll capture in the SOW if we proceed.
[10:03] Aisha Khan: thanks. last thing — how do you recommend we set the success criteria for the pilot?
[10:07] Priya Nambiar: practical recommendation: 1) validate p95 under spike load for chosen model <120ms, 2) quality regression <2% on your eval set, 3) KV cache hit rate > 20% for repeated contexts, 4) no telemetry exfiltration, logs verified in customer S3. those map to pass/fail gates in the rollout plan.
[10:26] Sofia Park: good.
[10:28] Jordan Lee: recap — Jordan will send bench CSV and Optimize guide, Priya will provision dev Dedicated and supply bench runner, Carlos will supply traffic profile and firewall details. we'll target pilot start first week of December.
[10:42] Aisha Khan: perfect. thanks all.
[10:45] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar and docs.
[10:50] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings; the export labeled a few lines as Speaker 1 where attribution uncertain. Radar: good fit for dedicated pilot; customer requested Thales HSM integration and specific retention rules.
